MINUTES
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING
  JANUARY 21, 2025

  1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

  A regular meeting of the Park and Activities Commission of the City of Rolling Hills
  Estates was called to order at 7:04 p.m. at City of Rolling Hills Estates Council Chamber,
  4045 Palos Verdes Dr. N., Rolling Hills Estates, California, by CHAIR MCCORMICK.

  2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

  CHAIR MCCORMICK led those present in the Pledge of Allegiance.

  3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Pope, Ciarolla, Johnson, Holdsworth, Bain,
  Persichina and McCormick

  Commissioners Absent:  None

  City Staff Present:  Maintenance Superintendent Mike Goldsmith
  Community Services Supervisor Rosa Pinuelas
  Community Services Coordinator Matt Morrow

  4.  PRESENTATION

  A.  PARK AND ACTIVITES COMMISSION REORGANIZATION PRESENTATION

  Supervisor Pinuelas stated that the City Council appointed COMMISSIONER
  PERSICHINA as Chair and COMMISSIONER POPE as Vice Chair of the
  COMMISSION.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK was recognized for his service as 2024 Chair of
  the Commission and was provided a plaque for his service.

  5.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  PARK & ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING DRAFT MINUTES OF
  DECEMBER 17, 2024

  COMMISSIONER BAIN made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER
  MCCORMICK to:

  APPROVE THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF
  DECEMBER 17, 2025.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  1
January 21, 2025
   There being no objection, CHAIR PERSICHINA so ordered.

  6.  AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA

  NONE.

  7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A.  STREET ENTRYWAY BEAUTIFICATION PROGRAM FUNDING REQUEST
  FROM ROLLING HILLS COUNTRY CLUB ESTATES HOMEOWNERS
  ASSOCIATION

  Superintendent Goldsmith gave a brief overview of the Street Entryway
  Beautification request from the Rolling Hills Country Club Estates Homeowners
  Association (as per the agenda materials).

  COMMISSIONER POPE commented that she liked the signage selected for the
  project.

  Supervisor Pinuelas stated that a budget adjustment has been submitted to cover
  the $2,500 in matching funds to the Rolling Hills Country Club Estates
  Homeowners Association (HOA), in response to COMMISSIONER BAIN.

  Superintendent Goldsmith stated that the HOA will pay the balance of the project
  costs not covered by the grant, in response to COMMISSIONER BAIN.

  Supervisor Pinuelas noted that the HOA selected the highest bid presented, in
  response to CHAIR PERSICHINA.

  VICE CHAIR POPE made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER BAIN TO
  APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE THE ROLLING HILLS COUNTRY CLUB ESTATES
  HOMEOWNERS ASSOCIATION REQUEST OF $2,500 IN MATCHING
  FUNDS FROM THE CITY’S STREET ENTRYWAY BEAUTIFICATION
  PROGRAM IN FY 2024-2025.

  AYES:  Ciarolla, Johnson, Holdsworth, Bain, McCormick, Pope, Persichina
  ABSENT:  None

  **ADJOURNED TO PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION ADVISORY BOARD MEETING AT
  7:10 PM**

  B.  ADVISORY BOARD REVIEW OF PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION ANNUAL
  REPORT

PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  2
January 21, 2025
   Supervisor Pinuelas gave a brief overview of the Pepper Tree Foundation Annual
  Report (as per the agenda material).

  In response to VICE CHAIR POPE, Supervisor Pinuelas stated that the higher than
  usual expenditures in the Equestrian Related Uses category was a result of a
  payment for the Ernie Howlett Arena 2 renovation project and that revenues
  spanned two fiscal years.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN asked about the Adopt-A-Trail balance reflected in the
  Statement of Fund Balance. CHAIR PERSICHINA stated that he believed that the
  Adopt-A-Trail category goes back 10 to 15 years but was unsure of the specific
  program. COMMISSIONER BAIN noted that there must be a lingering balance
  currently with that category. Supervisor Pinuelas stated that Staff would look into
  the Adopt-A-Trail category.

  Supervisor Pinuelas stated that Staff is currently working with the fundraising
  committee and developing a list of prospective donors for large donations for the
  Nature Center project to help close the anticipated funding gap due to the projected
  increase of construction costs of the project, in response to COMMISSIONER
  BAIN.

  **RECONVENED PARKS AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING AT 7:20 PM**

  C.  2024 PENINSULA PARADE OF LIGHTS DEBRIEF

  Coordinator Morrow gave a brief overview of the 2024 Peninsula Parade of Lights
  Debrief report (as per the agenda material).

  COMMISSIONER JOHNSON asked whether there was a large amount of repeat
  parade participants in this year’s parade compared to last year’s parade.
  Coordinator Morrow responded that he believed there were many repeat
  participants this year.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN commended Staff on another great parade.

  D.  2025 CONCERT IN THE PARK EVENT

  Coordinator Morrow gave a brief overview of the 2025 Concert in the Park event
  (as per the agenda material).

  The COMMISSION discussed potential genres for selection of the band and
  recommended a multi-genre cover band or a Motown/R&B band.

  VICE CHAIR POPE asked about how Staff finds bands to perform at the concert
  and if Staff looks into local talent and youth at the high schools who have bands.
  Coordinator Morrow stated that he typically looks at the bands that have been used

PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  3
January 21, 2025
   for other local cities’ Concert in the Park events in past years when searching for
  a band to perform at the event.

  Coordinator Morrow stated that he typically looks at the City of Manhattan Beach,
  City of Torrance, and City of Rancho Palos Verdes band selections for past concert
  in the parks as a starting point, in response to CHAIR PERSICHINA.

  Coordinator Morrow stated that he believes the crowd size has been relatively
  good since Staff have started offering different genres of bands at this event, in
  response to COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK.

  VICE CHAIR POPE commented that looking into a more local band would possibly
  assist in bringing in more of the community to attend this type of event.

  VICE CHAIR POPE asked whether there was still a grant available through LA
  County to assist Staff with the expenditures of this event. Supervisor Pinuelas
  stated that there was an arts grant available, but she was not sure if the concert
  qualified for that grant. She noted that Staff would continue to look into the
  possibility of grant funds to assist with this event.

  The COMMISSION asked if there would be the opportunity to have multiple bands
  perform at the event. Staff stated they would look into it and contact the production
  company regarding the time needed for set-up and if their equipment would be
  compatible to having multiple bands perform at the event.

  E.  2025 SUMMER MOVIE NIGHT PROGRAM

  Coordinator Morrow gave a brief overview of the 2025 Summer Movie Night
  Program (as per the agenda material).

  The COMMISSION discussed potential movie options and recommended Moana
  2 and Sonic the Hedgehog 3.

  COMMISSIONER HOLDSWORTH suggested coordinating with the City of
  Rancho Palos Verdes to avoid conflicts such as showing the same movie during
  the same month. Coordinator Morrow stated that he would speak with them to
  confirm.

  F.  2025 PROPOSED PARK TOUR SCHEDULE

  Coordinator Morrow gave a brief overview of the 2025 proposed park tour schedule
  (as per the agenda material).

  VICE CHAIR POPE made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER BAIN to:

  APPROVE THE 2025 PROPOSED PARK TOUR SCHEDULE.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  4
January 21, 2025
   There being no objection, CHAIR PERSICHINA so ordered.

  8.  STAFF ITEMS

  A.  EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS INFORMATION (VERBAL REPORT)

  Supervisor Pinuelas gave a brief overview of the emergency preparedness
  information that was available on the city website.

  Superintendent Goldsmith stated that his crew conducts weed abatement around
  the City and works with the Los Angeles County Fire Department regarding certain
  areas that need to be maintained. He also stated that he would check with Cal
  Water regarding the fire hydrant checks around the City, in response to
  COMMISSIONER BAIN.

  B.  MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)

  NONE.
  9.  COMMISSION ITEMS

  A.  ADOPT-A-PARK (VERBAL REPORT)

  COMMISSIONER BAIN reported that there was a portion of fence at Silver Spur
  Park that was very worn. Superintendent Goldsmith responded that Staff is
  working with local Scouts to assist in the maintenance of the fence at Silver Spur
  Park. COMMISSIONER BAIN also suggested installing a picnic bench at the park.

  Staff confirmed that Silver Spur Little League’s baseball season would be starting
  at Ernie Howlett Park, in response to CHAIR PERSICHINA.

  B.  MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)

  VICE CHAIR POPE asked if there was an opportunity to establish a program to
  recognize active service members or veterans with banners on street light poles
  along Silver Spur Road in the business district of the City. COMMISSIONER
  JOHNSON stated that this type of program may take some time to get established.
  The COMMISSION suggested that Staff look into the possibility and what it would
  entail to have this type of program.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK asked if there was a way to install a wooden
  seesaw at Founder’s Park. Superintendent Goldsmith stated that any type of play
  equipment would need to be purchased and installed by a licensed company.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  5
January 21, 2025
   COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK suggested staff conduct outreach to ask local
  HOAs what type of project may be best for the open land near George F. Canyon
  Nature Preserve.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK suggested holding an open house event to
  promote the parks and department programs while getting people out to the parks.

  10.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF DECEMBER 10, 2024

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

  11.  FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  A.  ASSESSMENT OF SPACE FOR POTENTIAL DOG PARK AND FUTURE PARKS

  NONE.

  12.  ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIR PERSICHINA ADJOURNED THE MEETING AT 7:49 PM TO THE NEXT
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING ON FEBRUARY 18, 2025, AT
  7:00 P.M., WHICH WILL BE HELD AT CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER AT CITY HALL.

  There being no objection, so ordered.

  Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

  __________________________  __________________________
  Matt Morrow  Lou Persichina
  Community Services Coordinator  Chair, Park & Activities Commission

PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  6
January 21, 2025
